artworks.title: The Death of Chione
artworks.description: Poussin stages Artemis' arrow through Chione's tongue — Daedalion's daughter punished for ranking her beauty above the goddess. Not Chione daughter of Boreas.

artworks.title: Diana Killing Chione
artworks.description: Tempesta's Metamorphoses plate: Diana's arrow strikes Chione while Autolycus and Philammon look on — the twin sons Apollo and Hermes fathered the same night.

artworks.title: Artemis and Chione
artworks.description: Carpioni's Blanton canvas pairs the huntress with her victim — Chione of Daedalion's house as Venetian Baroque myth.

artworks.title: Chione Killed on the Hunt by Offended Diana
artworks.description: Schou's Danish history-painting restages Ovid: Chione fallen under Diana's anger — the blasphemy that drives Daedalion toward the hawk.

artworks.title: Apollo and Mercury Visit Chione
artworks.description: Print of the double visitation: Apollo and Hermes both claim Chione in one night — Philammon and Autolycus as her twin divine gifts before Diana's arrow.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book 11: Chione boasts against Diana, is shot through the tongue, and Daedalion leaps from Parnassus — her death the hinge of the hawk metamorphosis.

popCulture.title: Chione (daughter of Daedalion)
popCulture.description: Daughter of Daedalion; mother of Autolycus by Hermes and Philammon by Apollo — not Chione daughter of Boreas.
